title: Brackets Round Negatives
idea: When you substitute, the number goes in brackets, sign and all, so a negative input is squared or multiplied correctly; then brackets, powers, × and ÷, + and −.
misconceptions: Squares without brackets, so the sign comes out wrong
Drops the sign of the input

estimate.basis: 150 spoken words a minute, plus each pause, 0.8 s for each cue and 2 s for each tap question with its longer feedback line. The two figures are the two recall versions; with no prerequisite explainer there is one recall version, so they are the same. Player turns are player-paced and not counted.

notes: Foundations is prior learning (FAL-953), so this runs 4–6 minutes, not 6–8, and some sections are short.

No prerequisite explainer. The recall section is one tap question on what students bring from earlier school (a negative times a negative), with no callback line, so it has a single `beats` list instead of `watched` and `not_watched`, and both length figures are the same.

No second-method section: the map lists no methods. The lesson's four (bracket-first, order of operations, top-and-bottom, estimate-check) are all here except top-and-bottom, which needs a fraction input and is left to the question type.
Example 3 is a two-part course-style item (SL2.2 function notation), as FAL-953 allows for Foundations.
Live numbers for the turns come from fn-pre-substitute (game/engine/situations/substitute.gd); the fallbacks are fixed and worked below.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Kia ora, welcome to the Scrapworks. I'm Tess. If it's broken, it ends up in my yard, and most of it goes back out the gate working. Most of it.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: A trader brought this counting drum back this morning. Says it's broken, because it told him minus three squared is minus nine.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: He's out front on my chilly bin, waiting for an apology. From a drum.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Thing is, the drum might be right. So might he. It all comes down to brackets.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: First, one you brought with you from school. Tap the answer.

right.speaker: tin-can-tess
right.say: Twelve. A negative times a negative is positive. Hang on to that one.

not_yet.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_yet.say: A negative times a negative is positive, and four threes are twelve. So it's plus twelve. Hang on to that one.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Here's the drum, opened up. A letter in an expression is a slot. When you substitute, you take the letter out and put a number in its place.

board.write: substitute: replace the letter with the number, in brackets

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Say the slot is x squared, and the number going in is minus three. The whole minus three goes in, not the three on its own. So it goes in with brackets round it. Minus three times minus three: plus nine.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: I fitted a bolt once and left the washer on the bench. Held fine, right up until the panel rattled off halfway out the gate.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: The minus sign is the washer. It goes in with the number, every time, and the brackets hold them together.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Now the drum. With no brackets, minus three squared means square the three first, then put the minus on. The power goes before the minus.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: So the drum read it with no brackets and said minus nine. The trader meant the brackets and wanted nine. Both right, for different questions.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: That's the order of operations doing its job. Brackets first, then powers, then times and divide, then plus and minus.

board.write: order of operations: brackets, powers, × and ÷, then + and −

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Bits on the bench, then. The number goes in with its brackets. Then the order.

problem.setup: Find the value of x² + 5 when x = −3.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Step one: what we're finding. The value of x squared plus five, when x is minus three.

board.write: Find the value of x² + 5 when x = −3.
board.label: Step 1: what are we finding?

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Step two: substitute. Take x out, and put minus three in, brackets and all.

choices: So the whole −3 is squared, sign and all

right.speaker: tin-can-tess
right.say: That's it. The minus goes in with the three, and the brackets keep them together.

not_yet.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_yet.say: The brackets mean the whole minus three gets squared, sign and all. Without them, only the three would be.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Step three: the order, and the power goes first, so minus three, in brackets, squared, is nine, and then you add the five and you've got fourteen.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Step four: the answer. When x is minus three, x squared plus five is fourteen.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Then check the sign. A square is never negative, so x squared plus five can't come out under five, and fourteen doesn't. Sweet as.

intro.speaker: tin-can-tess
intro.say: Your go. Same job, new numbers. Brackets on first.

fallback.setup: Find the value of x² + 7 when x = −4.

right.speaker: tin-can-tess
right.say: You kept the brackets. That's the whole trick, right there.

right.speaker: tin-can-tess
right.say: Sweet as. Bits on the bench, and it all went together.

not_yet.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_yet.say: Back on the bench with it. Can a square come out negative?

not_yet.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_yet.say: Put the number in with its brackets, then do the power first.

problem.setup: Find the value of 2x² − 5x when x = −2.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Bit harder now. Two x squared, minus five x, when x is minus two. Two slots this time, and both get minus two, in brackets.

board.write: Find the value of 2x² − 5x when x = −2.

right.speaker: tin-can-tess
right.say: Eight. Square first, so four, then double it.

not_yet.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_yet.say: Power before the times. Minus two, in brackets, squared, is four, and two fours are eight.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Next slot is minus five times minus two, and that's negative times negative, so plus ten. Eight and ten, eighteen.

problem.setup: The function f is defined by f(x) = 4 + 2x − x².

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Now one laid out the way the exam papers do it, with a part a and a part b. Write each letter down before you start on it, so whoever marks it can find your working.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Part a says write down, so no working needed. Zero goes in for x, and everything with an x in it disappears. f of zero is four.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Part b says find, so the working goes down. Every x gets minus three, in brackets.

choices: Square first, then the minus in front

right.speaker: tin-can-tess
right.say: Right. The bracket squares to nine, and the minus in front was never inside it.

not_yet.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_yet.say: The square goes first: minus three, in brackets, squared, is nine. The minus in front sits outside the bracket, so it's minus nine.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: So it's four, minus six, minus nine. Minus eleven.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Quick check on the sign. The only bit adding is the four, and the six and the nine take away more than that, so a minus answer makes sense.

board.write: Check: 4 is the only positive term, and 6 + 9 > 4, so f(−3) < 0 ✓

sections.misconception: Squares without brackets, so the sign comes out wrong

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Somebody left this on my bench. One line's a bit off. Find it.

ask.prompt: Tap the line with the slip.

right.speaker: tin-can-tess
right.say: That's the one. The minus four went in with no brackets, so only the four got squared.

not_yet.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_yet.say: Look at where the minus four goes in. Has every slot got brackets?

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: And you can catch it without redoing anything. x squared is a square, and a square is never negative, so that first bit can't ever be minus sixteen.

board.write: Check: x² ≥ 0, so x² can't be −16 ✗

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Line through it, and go again with the brackets on. Sixteen, minus eight. Eight.

intro.speaker: tin-can-tess
intro.say: Your go, and no help on the first try. Label your parts, and brackets round every number that goes in.

fallback.setup: The function g is defined by g(x) = 5 − 3x − x².

right.speaker: tin-can-tess
right.say: Choice. Parts labelled, and the minus kept outside the bracket.

right.speaker: tin-can-tess
right.say: That'd hold. I'd put it out front with a price on it.

not_yet.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_yet.say: Back on the bench with part b. What's minus two, in brackets, squared?

not_yet.speaker: tin-can-tess
not_yet.say: Look at the minus in front of the x squared. Is it inside the bracket, or outside?

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: So. When you substitute, the number goes in with its brackets, sign and all. Then brackets, powers, times, plus, in that order. Then check the sign makes sense.

board.write: Substitute: the number goes in brackets, sign and all
3. Check the sign and the size

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: Next time we run it the other way. You know what comes out, and you find what went in.

beats.speaker: tin-can-tess
beats.say: The trader's drum? Fine all along. I stuck a pair of brackets on the side and charged him for the repair. Best money I've made all week.
